evidence:
DIMENSION WEIGHTS: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty): [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. This matches the SKILL.md delivery profile ('Reward is shaped - functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2') and the Internal sheet annotation on row 44 ('Functionality has 60 pecent'). task/tests/tools/score.py is identical to the template: reward = weighted mean only if gates pass and functional > 0.05, else 0.0. No [judge].weight key exists in any judge.toml (only per-criterion weights). Maximum non-functional contribution is 0.4 (< 0.6 functional); pure style (visual, five likert craft rows each weight 1.2, sum 6.0) is capped at 0.2 of reward, and the floor zeroes a functionally dead app's polish/visual. Gates carry weight 1.0 per criterion only inside all_pass aggregation (gates/render/judge.toml:21, gates/constraints/judge.toml:21) and contribute 0.0 to the reward.

PER-CRITERION WEIGHTS (re-derived with tomllib): functional 43 criteria, sum 58.5, range 0.5-2.5; polish 5 criteria, sum 12.0, range 1.5-3; visual 5 likert, sum 6.0, all 1.2. Functional weights track what each row proves: the highest weights (2.5) go to stale-move refusal naming the actor (hro_stale_refused, functional/judge.toml:198), the live board within 15 s (hro_live_board :288) and candidate privacy (hro_candidate_private :387) - exactly the brief's stated 'hard part' (instruction.md:1,3,5,9). Multi-card/undo integrity rows (hro_bulk_all_or_none 2, hro_undo_restores 2, hro_undo_conflict 2), earlier-messages paging (2), unread counts (2), scrolled-up notice (2) and drafts (2) are also high. Low weights (0.5) go to narrow or trivially-adjacent rows: hro_job_open :27, hro_add_candidate :36, hro_reject_hired :90, hro_undo_full :126, hro_activity_refusals :270, hro_candidate_linked :396. Negative/refusal rows that a dead app could otherwise farm each name a successful control (e.g. hro_undo_conflict 'A successful undo earlier is the control', hro_observer_readonly 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control', hro_candidate_private 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'), so their weight is not earned by doing nothing. hro_refused_put_back (weight 2, :135) bundles real stage/place, reason and focus - all public (instruction.md:3; hireops_rules.md:85) - not a style item. No functional criterion grades styling or code structure.

POLISH: unlike the template's mobile/a11y/feedback rows, the task's polish dimension grades concurrency robustness the brief calls out (instruction.md:5,7: no closing the open card, wiping the note, moving the cursor; draft survives sign-out). Weights 3/3/2/1.5/2.5 rank the two live-preservation rows highest, consistent with the brief's emphasis. Both live-preservation rows score 0 if no live update arrives (polish/judge.toml:23,32), which correctly prevents a non-live app from collecting preservation credit for doing nothing (REVIEW_POLICY 'A negative needs a successful control'); this couples ~0.1 of reward to live delivery that functional also grades (2.5/58.5), but the preserved-state outcome is a distinct public promise, so it is not dishonest double-counting.

WEAK-APP REASONING: (a) A pretty but barely functional app passing only hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_add_email_rules and hro_candidate_linked (3.0/58.5 = 0.0513 > floor) could earn up to 0.6*0.0513 + 0.2*visual ~= 0.23 with polish near 0 (polish rows need live updates/conversations); a moderately functional but ugly app at functional ~0.35 gets ~0.21 + low visual. This is a consequence of the frozen template 0.6/0.2/0.2 and 0.05 floor (not task-editable; it belongs to rows 42/43), not of task-specific weight choices. (b) A conforming alternative that hides forbidden controls is not penalized: rows explicitly allow hiding with replay as the test (hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_other_job), so weight is not spent on a UI-shape preference.

MINOR OBSERVATION (not a defect): hro_job_open (0.5) carries five validation refusals plus independent-context visibility; its weight is light relative to content, but job/card creation is also an implicit precondition of nearly every other functional row and of the browser gate, so the effective weight of basic CRUD is much higher than 0.5.

RISK: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' Weight honesty here is established statically; no measured reward discrimination or ordering run confirms how these weights spread real partial apps. That required runtime evidence is missing, so risk=true. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
